components.label: Subscriber
components.responsibility: Submit authenticated plan and cancellation commands.

components.label: Subscription billing
components.responsibility: Expose explicit billing and access states while remote payment is asynchronous.

components.label: Command API
components.responsibility: Authorize accounts, compare expected versions and retain command receipts.

components.label: Subscription and invoice ledger
components.responsibility: Own local versions, period identities, immutable invoice amounts and durable outbound intent.

components.label: Renewal planner
components.responsibility: Claim due billing periods by durable unique key and catch up missed timers.

components.label: Payment dispatcher
components.responsibility: Execute committed intents with stable provider idempotency keys and bounded retries.

components.label: Payment processor
components.responsibility: Own payment-method tokens and authoritative charge receipts; support explicit idempotency retention limits.

components.label: Verified event inbox
components.responsibility: Persist signed event IDs before acknowledging; duplicates are harmless.

components.label: Payment reconciler
components.responsibility: Fetch authoritative object state when events are missing or reordered; compare local transition versions.

components.label: Entitlement projection
components.responsibility: Project accepted local billing versions into explicit grace/expiry policy.

components.label: Durable billing workflow
components.responsibility: Serialize commands and durable timers per subscription while remote payment is a retryable activity.

components.label: Workflow and invoice journal
components.responsibility: Persist workflow decisions and unique invoice identities atomically; never place a remote call inside a database transaction.

components.label: Settlement sweeper
components.responsibility: Reconcile pending provider objects and expired leases, respecting invoice identity and cancellation policy.

requirements.text: Authorize subscription commands and apply stable idempotency identities to invoice/payment attempts.
Define trial, active, past-due and canceled states, effective dates and access policy.
Handle duplicated, reordered or missing provider events and reconcile uncertain remote effects.
Recover renewals and cancellations after worker failure without charging the same invoice twice.

problem.scope: Recurring billing with payment-method tokens, plan changes, cancellation and asynchronous provider outcomes. Compare a relational subscription authority with durable per-subscription workflows. The payment provider is the charge authority; no raw card storage, universal ordering or exactly-once external calls are assumed.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Signature verification, duplicates, retries and event ordering limits.
references.title: Stripe webhook delivery

references.supports: Asynchronous subscription and invoice lifecycle notifications.
references.title: Stripe subscription events

references.supports: Concurrent state transitions and atomic durable intent.
references.title: PostgreSQL transaction isolation

acceptanceCases.given: One Start command is accepted but the UI times out.
acceptanceCases.then: Return the original result once; deny cross-account access.
acceptanceCases.when: Repeat the same command ID, then submit an unauthorized account request.

acceptanceCases.given: Two timers or recovery workers process the same billing period.
acceptanceCases.then: The unique invoice identity is shared; dispatches retain the same provider attempt identity.
acceptanceCases.when: Attempt to issue and dispatch the renewal concurrently.

acceptanceCases.given: The provider succeeds but dispatch acknowledgement is lost.
acceptanceCases.then: Reconcile the provider object or reuse the key within its documented retention; do not blindly create a second charge.
acceptanceCases.when: Expire the lease and restart processing.

acceptanceCases.given: A succeeded notification precedes an older failed event, and either is duplicated.
acceptanceCases.then: Local financial state converges to authoritative status and the event inbox deduplicates receipts.
acceptanceCases.when: Process both and fetch current provider state.

acceptanceCases.given: A cancel command advances cancellation epoch while payment is processing.
acceptanceCases.then: Record the settlement and explicit refund/credit policy without restoring access to the canceled version.
acceptanceCases.when: Receive a later payment success for the previous epoch.

guarantees: The same period and adjustment create one invoice identity; retries retain remote intent identity.
Financial settlement and entitlement are separate; stale events cannot bypass cancellation policy.

apis.errors: 403 wrong account; 409 version conflict; 422 invalid transition

assumptions: Provider tokens replace card details; this design does not establish payment-compliance certification.
Access grace, proration and cancellation policy are product choices fixed per version.
solutions.chooseWhen: A relational authority and a small number of background jobs fit the lifecycle.

stages.explanation: Begin with subscriber and a billing boundary; pending means accepted intent, not paid access. A timeout never creates a new invoice identity when the same command is retried. [A payment provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payment_service_provider) performs external financial effects that local retries cannot undo. Request identity, confirmed outcomes, and reconciliation are needed when a request times out after submission.
invariants: A timeout never creates a new invoice identity when the same command is retried.
stages.question: What can the UI promise after Start is accepted?
stages.reason: Begin with subscriber and a billing boundary; pending means accepted intent, not paid access.
stages.title: Separate request from payment success

stages.explanation: Expand the coarse boundary into command processing and durable state. Each accepted command compares or serializes one subscription version. [A payment provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payment_service_provider) performs external financial effects that local retries cannot undo. Request identity, confirmed outcomes, and reconciliation are needed when a request times out after submission. Consider this case: One Start command is accepted but the UI times out.
invariants: Each accepted command compares or serializes one subscription version.
stages.question: Who owns subscription versions and invoices?
stages.reason: Expand the coarse boundary into command processing and durable state.
stages.title: Expose command authority and ledger

stages.explanation: A renewal planner claims due periods using a unique subscription/period identity. Invoice amount and currency are fixed at issuance; adjustments have separate identities. [A payment provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payment_service_provider) performs external financial effects that local retries cannot undo. Request identity, confirmed outcomes, and reconciliation are needed when a request times out after submission.
invariants: Invoice amount and currency are fixed at issuance; adjustments have separate identities.
stages.question: How does a restart avoid a second renewal invoice?
stages.reason: A renewal planner claims due periods using a unique subscription/period identity.
stages.title: Define billing periods and invoices

stages.explanation: Commit payment intent before dispatch; send stable attempt identities to the provider. A local transaction cannot make a remote charge atomic with its commit. [A payment provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payment_service_provider) performs external financial effects that local retries cannot undo. Request identity, confirmed outcomes, and reconciliation are needed when a request times out after submission.
invariants: A local transaction cannot make a remote charge atomic with its commit.
stages.question: What happens if charging succeeds but the response is lost?
stages.reason: Commit payment intent before dispatch; send stable attempt identities to the provider.
stages.title: Add retryable payment activities

stages.explanation: Verify signatures against raw request bytes, persist the event ID, then acknowledge and process asynchronously. A 2xx webhook response means durable receipt, not completed subscription projection. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call.
invariants: A 2xx webhook response means durable receipt, not completed subscription projection.
stages.question: How are duplicate or forged webhooks handled?
stages.reason: Verify signatures against raw request bytes, persist the event ID, then acknowledge and process asynchronously.
stages.title: Persist verified event delivery

stages.explanation: Read the current provider object and apply an allowed versioned local transition instead of trusting event arrival order. Do not compare unrelated event timestamps as a global order; fetch authoritative status for ambiguity. [A payment provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payment_service_provider) performs external financial effects that local retries cannot undo. Request identity, confirmed outcomes, and reconciliation are needed when a request times out after submission.
invariants: Do not compare unrelated event timestamps as a global order; fetch authoritative status for ambiguity.
stages.question: Can an old failure event undo a confirmed payment?
stages.reason: Read the current provider object and apply an allowed versioned local transition instead of trusting event arrival order.
stages.title: Reconcile authoritative payment objects

stages.explanation: Separate financial settlement from access; cancellation epochs and effective dates fence stale activation. A late paid invoice may require refund or credit, but cannot silently reactivate a canceled version. [A race condition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_condition) makes an outcome depend on which operation finishes first. Responses need an identity or generation check so an older request cannot overwrite newer user intent.
invariants: A late paid invoice may require refund or credit, but cannot silently reactivate a canceled version.
stages.question: What does a late payment mean after cancellation?
stages.reason: Separate financial settlement from access; cancellation epochs and effective dates fence stale activation.
stages.title: Project cancellation and access policy

stages.explanation: Sweep pending intent and expired leases, reconcile provider objects and resume unissued periods. Respect remote idempotency retention; outside it, reconcile before retrying an uncertain charge. [A payment provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payment_service_provider) performs external financial effects that local retries cannot undo. Request identity, confirmed outcomes, and reconciliation are needed when a request times out after submission.
invariants: Respect remote idempotency retention; outside it, reconcile before retrying an uncertain charge.
stages.question: What if timers, events or dispatch acknowledgements are missing?
stages.reason: Sweep pending intent and expired leases, reconcile provider objects and resume unissued periods.
stages.title: Recover timers and uncertain settlement

solutions.title: Transactional ledger and asynchronous payment outbox
tradeoffs: Timers, leases and outbox recovery need explicit transactional implementation.
Multi-step changes require state transitions rather than a blocking request chain.
